answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, delivery risk is the binding constraint, and memory_c2 shows the low-cost alternative missed SLA in three of four quarters—unacceptable for a critical line without a second source in place. Memory_c4 and memory_c6 show renegotiating with the incumbent (benchmarking market rates, considering longer-term volume commitments) has recovered real margin and cut unit cost without narrowing service scope or introducing migration risk, directly addressing the 18% cost mandate while preserving continuity ahead of the 14-day contract expiration. I verify memory_c4 (renegotiation outcome) and memory_c2 (switch-vendor SLA risk) since they are the two most decision-critical and highest-stakes claims to confirm before committing scarce sourcing capacity this cycle. Switching primary vendor or adding a second source are deferred to next review rather than rushed under this timeline; a full multi-year lock-in is also avoided pending confirmation of memory_c4's magnitude, preserving some flexibility.
